title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Flight Controller's Log. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Flight Controller's Log
options.lineage: Working flight logs and handwritten mission checklists
options.thesis: Ten historic flights become one clear, hand-kept record.
options.viewport: A narrow flight log frames one mission question, four answer rows, the live score, and the next step.
options.risk: Can feel like homework unless each answer lands with a lively flight-status mark.

raised.raise: The ten entries form one finite sortie, with an unmistakable final landing.
Question number, progress, and score keep a steady alignment throughout the run.
Every state gets a readable label as well as color; none are coded by color alone.

options.label: Crewed-Mission Passport
options.lineage: Family travel passports and collected entry stamps
options.thesis: Each correct answer earns a stamp on a ten-stop spaceflight itinerary.
options.viewport: A passport page pairs a single mission question with a small itinerary; answers add a clearly labeled travel mark.
options.risk: The travel metaphor must stay secondary to the historical mission facts.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.lineage: Friendly consumer apps with generous touch controls
options.thesis: A welcoming quiz interface makes every choice easy to spot and use.
options.viewport: A centered question sits above four spacious answer controls and one unmistakable action.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: especially approachable and clear for a family audience; less distinctively about historic flight.
options.risk: Could read as a generic quiz if mission details do not lead.

options.label: Flight-Path Map
options.thesis: A plotted route makes progress through the mission sequence tangible.
options.viewport: One question is the active checkpoint; the progress line marks the route already flown.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: route markers clarify sequence and progress, while a map can distract from the mission facts.
options.risk: The map must remain a quiet wayfinding aid rather than become the content.

options.label: Split-Flap Departure Board
options.lineage: Rail concourse boards and their live departure rows
options.thesis: Historic flights arrive in a crisp, memorable mission sequence.
options.viewport: A board-like title and flight number lead into one clearly separated question and its choices.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: the departure sequence evokes real missions, but board language is less natural for answering a quiz.
options.risk: Character-flip motion must never delay or obscure an answer.

options.label: Cassette J-Card
options.thesis: A tightly sequenced tracklist gives the quiz a finite, satisfying arc.
options.viewport: A side-A-like list moves through the ten questions, then flips to a final score.
options.case: Fuses poorly: tape-side conventions obscure the real mission chronology.
options.kept: Keep its finite-sequence discipline: the ten entries end in a clear final landing.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference Setting
options.lineage: Two-column reference editions with a marked centre rail
options.thesis: A stable alignment rail keeps question metadata in a consistent place.
options.viewport: A slim centre rail carries question number and score between compact text blocks.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a reference-edition layout asks too much reading effort of a family quiz.
options.kept: Keep the dependable alignment of question, score, and progress.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: A bold, minimal signal makes active flight status unmistakable.
options.viewport: A single mission record owns the field, with score and status as high-contrast marks.
options.case: Fuses poorly: coded and sparse controls hide too much from young learners.
options.kept: Keep strong contrast and give every state a plain-language label.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar, straightforward quiz interface, executed with care.
canonCard.viewport: A centered question card, progress bar, score, four answer buttons, and a results state.
canonCard.risk: Clear and familiar, but visually interchangeable with many quizzes.
